clue.text: A knot that holds things up

definitions.meaning: a kind of knot used to make a rope fast to a post or ring
a snag or minor difficulty that causes delay

explanation.definitionFit: A rope fastening is called by this name, and so is a small snag that delays progress.

clue.text: Temporary inexpensive headgear for a Gilbertian gondolier ?

definitions.text: Temporary inexpensive headgear for a Gilbertian gondolier

parts.words: Temporary inexpensive headgear for a Gilbertian gondolier
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers two gondoliers share a throne, so each gets only part of the royal headgear; the phrase is also an old coin

explanation.surface: A cheap hat is wanted for a gondolier in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: A HALF-CROWN was a pre-decimal British coin worth two shillings and sixpence, hence inexpensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing a kingdom means each ruler wears half of the royal regalia, and the term was also a British coin.

clue.text: Poison ? Sound the alarm-bell !

indicators.note: sound tells us the alarm signal's name is to be said out loud, not spelt

parts.note: a tocsin is an alarm bell

explanation.surface: Someone suspects poisoning and calls for the alarm to be rung.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous substance produced by a living organism is a natural venom.

clue.text: Bravery of foreign kings within the border

indicators.note: within says the kings sit inside the border

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
rois is French for kings

explanation.surface: Foreign monarchs show courage defending the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Great courage shown in the face of danger is valour.

clue.text: No eye-opener, this!

parts.note: an eye-opener is usually a revelation; read literally, the thing described makes the eyes close, sending you to sleep

explanation.surface: Something unsurprising is being dismissed as no revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleep-inducing drug or a dull speech is the opposite of something that keeps the eyes open.

clue.text: Dispensed with spring colour

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone gave up a spring shade of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To do without something is to forgo it, as when one is let off a duty.

clue.text: Ecclesiastes

parts.note: the book of the Bible whose narrator, Koheleth, is translated as one who addresses the congregation

explanation.definitionFit: Koheleth, the voice of the book, is rendered in English Bibles as the one who sermonises.

clue.text: A musical performance indeed !

definitions.meaning: a concert given by a soloist or small group
read as 'in deed': the part of a legal deed setting out the facts

explanation.definitionFit: A solo concert carries this name, and so does the statement of facts set out in a legal document.

clue.text: Bills I am putting in the dossier for reproduction

indicators.note: putting in says the bills and the I am go inside the dossier

parts.note: a file is a dossier
ACS, short for accounts, are bills
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone files invoices in a folder to have them copied.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact copy of a document is a reproduction of it.

clue.text: Between a find and a view for John Peel

definitions.text: Between a find and a view for John Peel

parts.words: Between a find and a view for John Peel
parts.note: the hunting song D'ye ken John Peel runs 'From a find to a ... from a ... to a view', the pause when hounds lose the scent

explanation.surface: Something comes between finding and seeing for a hunting man.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a Cumbrian huntsman celebrated in a famous English folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: In foxhunting the halt when hounds lose the scent comes after the fox is found and before it is sighted.

clue.text: Live Sybaris' style, being light-headed in Rome

definitions.text: Live Sybaris' style, being light-headed in Rome

parts.words: Live Sybaris' style, being light-headed in Rome
parts.note: Sybaris was an ancient Greek city famed for luxury; the verb wanted begins with the Latin word for light

explanation.surface: Someone lives a life of indulgence and grows giddy in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-headed in Rome' is not giddiness: the word's head, its first three letters, is LUX, Latin for light.
explanation.definitionFit: The citizens of Sybaris were proverbial for self-indulgence, so to live like them is to wallow in comfort.

clue.text: It's hidden many a pain

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone has concealed a great deal of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret store of goods or valuables is a hoard kept out of sight.

clue.text: Double dealing — for which one needs the Ace of Trumps ?

definitions.text: Double dealing — for which one needs the Ace of Trumps

parts.words: Double dealing — for which one needs the Ace of Trumps
parts.note: a swindle; at cards the ace of trumps gives you assurance and takes a round, so you need both trust and a won hand

explanation.surface: A card game is being described in which a sharp needs the top trump.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle that works by winning the victim's trust is a fraud built on misplaced faith.

clue.text: When Alfred Doolittle aimed to get to church

definitions.text: When Alfred Doolittle aimed to get to church

parts.words: When Alfred Doolittle aimed to get to church
parts.note: in My Fair Lady, Eliza's father sings that he must be got to the church punctually for his wedding

explanation.surface: A question about Eliza Doolittle's father heading for his wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolittle's song asks to be brought to the church punctually, at the appointed hour.

clue.text: Do they find their mates in Cardiff's bay ?

definitions.text: Do they find their mates in Cardiff's bay

parts.words: Do they find their mates in Cardiff's bay
parts.note: Cardiff's dockland was called Tiger Bay, so its females would be the big cats

explanation.surface: Sailors are asked whether they meet partners in the Welsh docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiger Bay was the dock district of Cardiff, the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Female big cats would naturally seek partners in a bay named after their kind.

clue.text: An occasion of inner satisfaction

parts.note: inner satisfaction sounds spiritual, but here it is the stomach being filled

explanation.surface: A moment of deep contentment is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour set aside for eating is when the belly gets filled.

clue.text: Cook's attempt

definitions.meaning: Captain James Cook's ship on his first voyage

explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook sailed to Australia in the ship of this name, and the word also means a strenuous try.

clue.text: Clear up and bring the change

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of bring the are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up and brings coins.
explanation.definitionFit: When weather clears it becomes lighter and sunnier.

clue.text: Turn a weapon on a member of the opposition for trifling

indicators.note: turning round the word for the weapon means writing its letters backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a British Conservative, then the party in opposition

explanation.surface: Someone aims a gun at an opposition politician over a petty matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' turns GUN into NUG; then A and TORY follow, with 'on' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless or of no force is of only petty, minor importance.

clue.text: The initial motive for anti-State activity

indicators.note: the initial of the word The is its first letter

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Someone asks what first drove a rebel's actions against the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or plotting against its ruler is the gravest crime against the state.

clue.text: A balmy region

parts.note: balmy suggests mild weather, but here it is the biblical land famed for its healing balm

explanation.surface: A place with a mild, pleasant climate is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible asks 'Is there no balm in' this land, a region east of the Jordan famous for its soothing resin.

clue.text: The days of Wellington and Bismarck ? That was long ago

definitions.text: The days of Wellington and Bismarck
definitions.meaning: Wellington was the Iron Duke and Bismarck the Iron Chancellor
the prehistoric period after the Bronze Age

explanation.definitionFit: Two leaders nicknamed for a metal suggest an era named for it, and that era is also a prehistoric period.

clue.text: West Indian about to be embraced by Mr. Porter

indicators.note: to be embraced by puts about inside the name of the songwriter

parts.note: Cole Porter, the American songwriter
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Caribbean man is about to be hugged by a songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of mixed European and African descent born in the Caribbean is so called.

clue.text: Gay but impecunious show ?

parts.note: John Gay wrote a famous ballad opera of 1728 about thieves and paupers; impecunious hints at the penniless title character

explanation.surface: A cheerful but cash-strapped theatrical production is described.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera is titled after a penniless street figure, so it is a show by Gay about poverty.

clue.text: Indian transport in the isles

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage in India

explanation.definitionFit: A horse cart in India and a South Pacific archipelago share the name.

clue.text: Bring into play, right under the river

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the right below the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Bring something into action on the right bank below the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert influence is to put it to use, applying force.

clue.text: Agreeable situations for fliers

parts.note: fliers suggests airmen in comfortable posts, but here it is birds in their homes

explanation.surface: Comfortable postings for pilots are described.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug, cosy berth is likened to a bird's home, and birds are the fliers that build them.

clue.text: An unconventional decorator's place in Paris

indicators.note: an unconventional arrangement of the letters of the decorator signals a rearrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An eccentric interior designer has a home in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's adds no letter; DECORATOR is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trocadéro is a well-known square and palace site in Paris facing the Eiffel Tower.

clue.text: Pass on ancestral traits, showing sound similarity

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the run of words Pass on ancestral

explanation.surface: Parents hand down family characteristics, revealing a likeness in voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' says the answer is on view inside pASS ON ANCEstral.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words is a similarity of sound, as in rhyme.

clue.text: Samson's meat provider

parts.note: Samson's riddle in Judges: 'Out of the devourer came forth meat', the honey found in a lion's carcass

explanation.surface: Someone supplied food to the biblical strongman.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson's riddle names the lion as the devourer out of which food came, so it was his source of meat.
